subject: Tenant site readiness & storage/network checklist for EdgeWave POC
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>

Cc: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-03-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Tenant site readiness & storage/network checklist for EdgeWave POC

Hi Daniel —

Thanks again for the walkthrough today. To make the on-prem POC smooth, I put together a short checklist that we need validated by your ops team before we schedule the site validation runbook:  

- Confirm site topology: number of racks, cross-connects, and whether there are separate VLANs for management, model data, and GPU traffic.
- Node pool plan: how many host nodes will be available for inference (CPU-only control plane vs GPU worker pools), GPU types, and per-rack power constraints.
- Storage plan: intended model storage (NFS/SMB/Isilon vs block store), local NVMe for KV/cache, and backup/retention expectations.
- Network egress & FW: outbound allowlist, NAT behavior, and proxy requirements for call-home/metrics.
- Security: KMS/HSM for key wrapping, audit-log export endpoint, and SOC2 related artifacts you can share.
- Ops windows & contact: proposed 2-day window for validation + escalation contact.

I've attached a lightweight node-pool sizing workbook that contains our suggested starting points for H100 and A100 fleets; it's deliberately conservative so we can right-size after telemetry. Logan and Marissa — feel free to flag anything we should change before we lock this with EdgeWave.

Next step for Daniel: if you can confirm the items above and drop the network drawing we can schedule a 2-hour site validation call.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Solutions PM | Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com

From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@edgewave.com>

Date: 2029-03-15T10:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Tenant site readiness & storage/network checklist for EdgeWave POC

Vanessa —thanks for the checklist. Quick answers from ops (high level):

- Topology: Two racks reserved in RackRoom-3 (both in the same L2/VRF). We can create 3 VLANs (mgmt/data/gpu). Cross-connect to our storage array is 25G.
- Node pools: Initial plan is 4 GPU hosts (per rack) — H100 80GB per server (we can swap to A100 if required). No concerns on power for 4 hosts/rack. Control plane will be a small 3-node CPU-only cluster.
- Storage: We run a central NetApp cluster for persistent model artifacts (NFSv4). We can also provision local NVMe on hosts for ephemeral KV cache.
- Egress/Firewall: Outbound only via a NAT with strict allowlist; we prefer explicit IPs to be whitelisted. No forward proxies.
- Security: We have an on-prem HSM (Luna) and can provide a KMS endpoint; audit logs ship to our SIEM over TLS.

I've uploaded the site network drawing (attached) and a sheet with exact rack power/cabinet IDs. We will need the required ports for model download/health checks called out (TCP 443 outbound to your ingestion endpoints) plus an allowlist for metrics ingestion (ports and targets in the drawing).

Can you confirm whether Redwood needs S3-compatible endpoints for blob staging or if NFS is sufficient for the POC?

—Daniel
EdgeWave Systems — Senior Ops Engineer

Vanessa / team — quick technical notes after reviewing the drawing and the node-sizing workbook: 

1) Storage classes & staging
- For the POC, we can operate directly against NFSv4 for model artifacts (read-mostly). We'll configure a "models-nfs" StorageClass (provisioner: nfs.csi.k8s.io) with a conservative accessMode ReadWriteMany. Production recommendation is to move to an S3-compatible object store for scalable checkpointing and multi-site replication, but not required for POC.
- Local NVMe: use host-local ephemeral volumes for the KV cache to maximize throughput and minimize latency. We'll configure the runtime to checkpoint to NFS periodically.

2) PVC layout (initial suggestion)
- Control plane: 3 x 40Gi PVCs (etcd + kube-system logs)
- Model artifacts (NFS-backed): StorageClass models-nfs, start with 2Ti provisioned (grow as needed).
- Worker node scratch: host-local NVMe 600Gi per GPU host for KV/cache + tmp artifacts.

3) CSI & drivers
- Use the standard NFS CSI for the NetApp export. Install the hostpath provisioner for ephemeral testing. For parity with our runtime, plan to test Ceph/Rook only if EdgeWave wants replication across racks.

4) Network & egress
- We'll request these outbound allowlist entries from EdgeWave: 3 IPs for telemetry endpoints (443), 1 IP for container image registry (depending on whether you mirror images), and SNI-based allow if NAT requires it. We will not insist on inbound firewall rules beyond SSH from their jump host for validation.

5) Security & KMS
- HSM integration: our agent supports KMIP and PKCS#11 for envelope encryption. For the POC, use a service account in the local KMS with a rolling key (we'll test key rotation during validation). Provide a network route to the HSM management endpoint.

I'll draft exact PVC YAMLs and a short validation playbook (node readiness, PV binding, model fetch/serving, KV cache stress). Marissa — can you take the runbook ownership? I'll attach the sample manifests to the HubSpot ticket.

—Logan
